about: The ADR-187 divergence ledger for SCALPEL (ADR-187 §5, started by ADR-189 / B355). Every intentional difference between the parity target (the composed engine) and an oracle it calls (the SCALPEL oracle; since B382 also SwarmSynth, reference/swarmsaw.html), one entry each; the order of the entries carries no meaning. A built entry sits behind its own engine flag, default 0 unless the entry says `default: 1` (B382, ADR-187 A1: a divergence the human ruled ON, one per PR; it carries `ruled`, and `moves` for each pinned scenario it changes at the defaults), so all flags off is the engine before the first divergence, bit for bit. Checked by tools/labharness/divergence_ledger_check.mjs (./verify fast): L1 shape, L2 the oracle blob, L3 each built flag exists at its ledgered default, L4 all off = the pinned fingerprints below and the defaults = the pins or the claimed moves, L5 each built flag changes a scenario, L6 each stays in its declared scope, L7 the engine's SwarmSynth patches and their entries are one set, L8 every divergence flag the engine has is a built entry's, L9 the entries' order changes no finding. A scope scenario is a preset name, or {preset, over, sr}, or that with a note `script` ("on <note>...", "off <note>...", "render <samples>"; B465) for a divergence that acts on event timing. Mirror policy (ADR-187, ratified): the composed engine IS the lab JS, so these are mirrored by construction; js_limit states what the browser cannot follow, or null.

divergences.description: First-order ADAA on a blade carrier, REPLACING the scanner's carrier-wrap PolyBLEPs, NARROWED by ADR-189 A1 to where it beats them: the carrier shape is not sine (nor sine->saw, which has no antiderivative), AND (the blade is an FM mode, 1 or 2, OR Band-limit is off), AND an FM blade's modulator is not S&H (mshape 7). Discrete per-blade parameters, no thresholds. Everywhere else the carrier keeps its BLEPs, bit for bit. The carrier sample becomes its mean over the phase swept since the previous internal sample, (F(cp) - F(cp0))/(cp - cp0) with the oracle's RazorCore.F; the midpoint below |cp - cp0| < 1e-7; the plain sample at blade entry. Half an internal sample of carrier-content lag, uncompensated (the engine header states why).

divergences.description: The onset lock (a note-start coupling burst, Kenv, decaying over dissolve) is BIPOLAR, the C++'s law (ADR-056): Kenv = 8*onset*|onset|, its positive part added to the sync target and 3x its negative part to the splay target (the x3 of the steady splay gain), so a negative onset is a SPLAY burst. SwarmSynth squares the sign away (Kenv = 8*onset^2), so onset -x played the same sync burst as +x, although the composed engine exposes onset -1..1. For onset >= 0 both laws are the same expressions (ADR-056's superset proof), so nothing there moves. Built as a text patch of SwarmSynth's noteOn and controlTick (the engine's SWARM_PATCHES); 0 is SwarmSynth's expression, character for character.

divergences.description: The blade's frame holds its course where the swarm's phase centre is undefined, and a member's lead reaches its blade as a ramp, never a step (ROADMAP B461; the human, 2026-10-12, heard a click inside one held note and saw it 'where the voices cross each other'). The oracle measures each member's lead from psi, the angle of the summed phase vectors, every 32 samples, and its render reads the lead at once; where the order parameter R passes through zero psi swings by up to half a cycle in one tick and every blade jumps. With the flag on each voice keeps a frame angle: every tick it advances by the members' mean phase advance (measured where the phases step, not predicted from the member frequencies, which the swarm moves every 16 samples), then moves toward psi by a fraction of the difference and by no more than 8 cycles per second (converted per tick from seconds). The fraction is g(R), rising linearly from 0 at R 0.05 to 1 at R 0.25, per REFERENCE tick of 32 samples at 48 kHz (1/1500 s); a tick of length dt takes 1 - (1 - g)^(dt / dtRef), so the frame closes on the centre in the same time at every sample rate, with g 0 giving 0 and g 1 giving 1 exactly. Where that correction is whole and inside the rate the frame is assigned psi itself, so in a locked swarm the leads' targets are the oracle's bit for bit. Each lead then travels to its value under the frame over the 32 samples of the tick, the shortest way round. A note's first tick sets the frame to psi and the leads outright (the oracle's law). A member that joins a held frame (N raised, or the flag turned on at a smaller N) has its lead set at the next tick, not ramped. Spread law 3 reads the lead under the frame, not its ramp: through spread(), as a step per tick, an exception to 'never as a step' that B460 owns. The three constants were set by ADR-216.

divergences.finding: (1) ACCEPTANCE 2 AS THE HUMAN RULED IT (2026-10-12, on the lead's recommendation: 'judge the fix with Position spread at 0, at both 1x and 2x oversampling. The present law must still read at least one jump there, so the test can see the fault. The pad-as-shipped row is printed but not judged, and becomes B460's test.'). With Position spread 0 the flag-on pad reads no isolated jump at C3, G3 or C4 at os 2 or at os 1, and the present law reads 3 / 1 / 2 and 5 / 2 / 4. The pad as shipped still reads 1 / 0 / 0 at os 2 and 3 / 0 / 0 at os 1 with the flag on: those are B460's steps (the residual above), and that row is B460's test. (2) After the frame has held through R near zero the measured centre is about half a cycle away, and the frame then turns to it at the rate limit: about 60 ms of every blade sweeping half a cycle, in place of the jump. (3) THE HALF-CYCLE TIE. Which way the frame turns on leaving a hold is the sign of its error there, and that error can sit on the half-cycle tie. At N 6 (the pad) it does not: the critic measured 12 exits with |error| 0.300 to 0.490 cycles, the least 0.00994 clear of the tie. At N 2 it always does: the summed phase vector lies on the two members' bisector, so every exit is half a cycle to within a rounding (measured: within 8.5e-15 of the tie on all 22 exits probed, either sign; the critic: 1e-16 to 4e-15), and the turn's direction is decided by that rounding. The C++ and the JS do not share sin, cos or atan2. Two N 2 parity rows were built and are HELD OUT of the committed scenario set until the human rules what the frame does after a crossing (ROADMAP B461): `C/D6 two members, detune 14` and `C/D6 two members, detune 30`, both the renderer's two-blade base (N 3, w 0.3, k 5.5, c 0.6, b2on 1, mode2 4, w2 0.2, k2 3, c2 0.35) with N 2, frame 1, phaseMode 2, law 0, driftRate 0.1, bspread 0.3, detune 14 (or 30), K 0.45, A 300, frameHold 1, snapped, seed 0xB385, 48 kHz, notes 45 and 52 at velocity 0.85 held for 900 blocks of 128 and released for 20. As written they hold parity (rms 2.8e-15 and 4.3e-15, max-abs 2.2e-13 and 2.8e-13, events identical); with the note frequencies moved 1 to 15 ULP on both sides (the renderer's --nudge) 2 of the 30 renders miss (detune 30 at 2 ULP: rms 2.7e-2, max-abs 0.61; detune 14 at 13 ULP: rms 2.8e-2, max-abs 0.64; events differ). They hold only where the two math libraries agree to the last bit, and CI's lanes run another one. No tie rule is built.

divergences.description: The feedback / cross-mod loop keeps the ORACLE'S TAP (the PolyBLEP output, render :840) and runs it through a one-pole low-pass at 5 kHz (LOOP_FC; a time constant in seconds, converted per internal sample). ADR-189 A1: the tap change first built (tapping the current sample) was DROPPED: it moved broad#828's rate-locked cycle from R/5 to R/3 instead of curing it, and made broad#857 A5 6.2 dB worse. Measured on broad#828 A1/E5 at os 1/2/4/8, the worst line over its local floor: off +19.4, 3 kHz +2.3, 4 kHz +1.3, 5 kHz +2.2, 6 kHz +3.4, 8 kHz +7.1; broad#540 (the other patch with the cycle): off +20.2, 4 kHz +1.6, 5 kHz +3.0. 5 kHz is the highest cutoff with every line within the +-3 dB scatter of a clean reference. Halving or quartering the loop gain leaves the cycle; os only moves it. The oracle's xin is overwritten in stepM before the blade step reads it.

divergences.description: The coupling smoother's per-tick coefficient comes from a time constant in SECONDS, B150's law in the C++ (SwarmCore(): 0.08 at 44.1 kHz exactly, else 1 - exp(-(16/sr)/kKsmTauSeconds), kKsmTauSeconds = 4.3512 ms, the value that gives 0.08 at 44.1 kHz), in place of SwarmSynth's literal 0.08 per 16-sample tick at every rate (an ADR-009 per-tick constant: 4.35 ms at 44.1 kHz, 4.00 ms at 48 kHz, 2.00 ms at 96 kHz). Resolved once per SwarmSynth, at construction, as the C++ does. 44.1 kHz is special-cased to the literal, as in the C++, because the round trip is three ULP short of 0.08. 48 kHz: 0.073746064208033535. divergences.description: The DEVICE default oversampling is os 1, and os 2 is the HQ setting. The SCALPEL oracle constructs at setOS(2), and the composed engine inherits that, so the product default now differs from the oracle's. It is a patch-default change, not an engine one: the SCALPEL lab's `DEF` is the oracle's constructor values with `LAB_DEF` written over them, and `LAB_DEF.os = 1` is the whole divergence. The engine core's setOS(2) (h2/engine/engine.h), every parity scenario and both self-digests stay at os 2, so no digest moves. Saved state is protected by its own `os` field (ADR-197 rule E): a record that carries `os` plays at it; a record with none (the factory presets, which the listening gate covered) plays at the new default. tools/labharness/os_default_check.mjs holds that and its must-fail controls.

oracle.sites: constructor :336 (this.os = 0; this.setOS(2)); the lab reads it through oracleDefaults() (scalpel-interface-lab.html, `{ os: REF.os }`)

divergences.target: docs/design/scalpel-interface-lab.html LAB_DEF.os (the device default); the engine core is unchanged
divergences.scope: the lab's boot, INIT, double-click reset and any preset that carries no `os` (0 of the 83 bench presets and the 12 envelope presets do); every preset that carries `os` is untouched

divergences.description: A taken voice fades (ROADMAP B459; the human, 2026-10-12, first playtest of the preview: 'Breathing Pad is very clicky'). With the pool full a poly note-on takes a voice that is still sounding (ADR-083 tier 2, the quietest releasing tail, or tier 3, the oldest held voice; the same picks at a voice cap) and restarts it as a fresh voice: the envelope keeps its level while the phases, filters and DC state reset, so the output jumps in one sample. With the flag on, a picked voice that is active with its envelope at or above 1e-3 is not restarted. Its sound fades to zero over 0.005 s (a linear gain ramp on top of its own envelope, the cull's arithmetic, counted in whole samples: 240 at 48 kHz, 221 at 44.1 kHz), the note waits in the voice, and it starts from silence at the exact sample the ramp ends, as a note on a free voice starts. The render cuts itself at that sample, so the start does not depend on the host's block size; the keep-phase snapshot a waiting note reads is taken at that cut, from the voice whose fade has just ended if it is the newest. While a note waits its voice is the note's: it carries the note's age from the take, the live count and the cap count it, tiers 1 and 2 pass it by, a retune reaches it as it reaches a started note (the played frequency moves, the struck one stays the glide target), a panic or a mode change cancels it (the fade runs out), and if tier 3 picks the voice again the newer note replaces the waiting one without restarting the fade. At a full cap with capPolicy 1, a waiting note that is the oldest held is cancelled and the new note takes the free slot. A voice already fading under the cull is taken over from its present gain, over the samples the cull had left or 0.005 s, whichever is shorter. Mono and legato are untouched, and a voice below 1e-3 restarts at once as before. TWO RULES PROPOSED FOR THE HUMAN TO RATIFY, which replace ADR-216's 'a note-off for the waiting note is remembered: the note starts, then releases at once' (measured: under that rule a note whose off came inside its wait was never heard, and the next note then took a HELD voice in its place): (a) A STOLEN NOTE KEEPS ITS GATE: an off that comes k samples after the take is remembered with k, and the note is released k samples after it starts (an off that comes after the note has started is an ordinary off); (b) A WAITING NOTE WHOSE OFF IS REMEMBERED IS A RELEASING TAIL TO THE TIERS, and the quietest: the next note takes its voice and replaces it, without restarting the fade, and held notes stay protected (ADR-083's point). The constant was set by ADR-216.

oracle.sites: noteOn() :368-379 (a voice taken from the pool is restarted at once); startVoice() :394-418 (`if (!v.active) v.env = 0`: a sounding voice keeps its level)

divergences.scope: poly note-ons that take a voice still sounding: a full pool, or a full voice cap. No preset is in or out of scope by its parameters: any patch reaches it once its pool is full, and none does before. So its scenarios here are note scripts (the ledger check's scripted form, B465): a chord struck over a releasing chord, with a pool of 3 (every voice is taken: in scope) and with the preset's own pool of 6 (free voices: out of scope)

metric.detector: tools/h2_steal_fade_check.mjs (./verify full), on the C++ engine through the harness: ledger/breathing-pad with its settings pinned (detune 14, K 0.45, law 0, A 1500, S 0.9, R 3000, N 6; and b2on 0 where a row needs it), triads (C F G Am Em Dm from C3) at velocity 0.85, each held 1.6 s and struck 0.1 s after the last release, 48 kHz, seed 1. The jump at a chord is the largest |difference| over the first four samples after its note-ons, on either channel, between a render with the chord and one without it (the same history, the same flag), as a share of the rms of the 50 ms before

jump.quietTails: a take of the QUIETEST tails at a pool of 6 and of 8 (blade 2 off). Flag off, pool 6, chords 3 to 6: 29.41 %, 12.23 %, 40.79 %, 15.23 %; pool 8: 12.14 %, 3.56 %, 14.39 %, 4.76 %. Flag on, pool 6: 0.227 %, 0.084 %, 0.058 %, 0.071 %; pool 8: 0.054 %, 0.040 %, 0.164 %, 0.045 %. Ceiling 0.5 %, PROPOSED (worst 0.227 %, about twice)
jump.poolTakenWhole: a pool of 3 taken whole, loud. Three tails 0.1 s after their release (tier 2): flag on 2.073 % (blade 2 off) and 1.793 % (blade 2 on), flag off 429.65 %; ceiling 3 %, PROPOSED (about one and a half times the worst). Three held voices (tier 3): flag on 0.794 % and 0.550 %, flag off 281.12 %; ceiling 1.5 %, PROPOSED (about twice). It is larger than at pool 6 because all the sound is under the ramp: over four samples a 240-sample ramp removes up to 3/240 of it
jump.freeVoices: chord 2 (no voice taken): 0.008 % with the flag on and off, at both pools; required under 1 %
jump.control: the flag-off reading must be at least 5 % at every taken chord at pool 6 and at each class of the pool taken whole

metric.fade: the fade itself, at the pool taken whole: the peak of the output over the ramp's last tenth (24 samples) over the peak of the 50 ms before the take: 0.032 to 0.041 (ceiling 0.08, PROPOSED, about twice the worst). Its must-fail runs on every run: the same job through the harness's control adapter control/steal-cut (h2/harness/control_steal.h, two shipped engines: the old sound unfaded for the fade's length, then cut) reads 0.585 to 0.626; the engine with the ramp's scaling really deleted reads 0.583 to 0.626 and turns the row red
metric.lateness: 240 samples (5.000 ms) at 48 kHz at every chord whose three notes all wait (seven at pools 6 and 8, four at the pool taken whole), to the sample: the first sample at which the render differs from the same render with the waiting notes cancelled by a panic. 221 samples at 44.1 kHz (the parity row). A culled tail that is taken waits 240 too (it waited 257 to 369 before the cap on the take-over)
metric.startStep: what the starting notes add over their first four samples: 0.0086 % to 0.0162 % of the level; ceiling 0.05 %, PROPOSED
metric.blockSize: host blocks of 16, 37 and 128 frames, flag on and off: bit-identical on the six chords at pool 6, and on four chords at a pool of 3 with keepPhase 1 and random start phases (with the keep-phase snapshot NOT taken at the cut that row reads 1.08 and 1.01 with the flag on). Of the 40 parity rows, 39 are bit-identical at blocks of 1, 16, 37, 128 and 1000; the one taken from under the cull carries the cull's known float32 dependence. A random-script fuzz (120 scripts, chopped at 1, 16 and 37 frames): none of the 60 scripts with no voice cap depends on the chop, flag on or off; with a cap 34 do with the flag off and 33 or 34 with it on, each one a script in which the cull or the steal policy's own fade ran
metric.monoLegato: bit-identical with the flag on and off (the check's two renders; and in the self-digests, `C/D7 mono, the flag on` has the digest of `C/FT chord on a mono voice in one block`, and the two legato rows share one)
metric.liveness: the flag-on six-chord renders are 0.31 dB (pool 6) and 0.13 dB (pool 8) under their flag-off twins: a restarted voice attacks from its old level, a waiting note from silence
metric.parity: 40 flag-on scenarios (C/D7 ...) at C++/JS parity: worst rms 1.4e-14, worst max-abs 5.8e-13, events and readouts identical
metric.cpu: not measured (Layer-E). With the flag off the cost is a few tests per voice per render call; while a steal's fade runs the engine renders one call per sample for its length (5 ms), as under the cull, and a render call is cut in two at each fade's end and at each kept gate's end

divergences.finding: (1) WHICH ROWS OF THE CHECK HAVE BLADE 2 OFF, AND WHY. The pad's second blade is a noise blade (mode2 3), which draws from the engine's shared random stream on every noise step while it renders; a note-on that starts a voice draws from the same stream. So a render with a chord and one without it hear different noise from the note-on onwards whenever the chord STARTS a voice there, taken voice or not, and a with/without comparison reads that as a jump. With the lead's seven settings and blade 2 on, a chord that takes NO voice read 2 % to 50 % depending on its notes and on the host seed (ROADMAP B459's row read 1 %), and one held note plus a note on a free voice read 0.007 % at C3 and 94 % at E3. So the free-voice control and every flag-off control are judged with blade 2 off (a free-voice start and a flag-off restart both draw at the note-on). A take draws nothing at the note-on, so the flag-on rows of a pool taken whole are judged with blade 2 on as well; the rows at pools 6 and 8 stay on the blade-2-off basis they were measured on, and their blade-2-on readings are printed unjudged on every run (chord 2, no voice taken: 50.3 %, and 17.4 % under spread law 4). (2) NOT CHASED: that noise blade's draws are themselves a way one note changes another's sound (every note-on re-seeds every other voice's noise from that sample on). It is not D7's. Nor is this, a fault of the engine with the flag off too: with keepPhase on, a note-on after full silence reads the snapshot left at the last host block boundary at which a voice still sounded. (3) Choices the ruling left open, accepted by the lead on 2026-10-13: the fade is counted in whole samples (round(0.005 * sr)); the old sound is released at the take; the waiting voice takes the note's age at the take and keeps it; notes whose fades end together start in the order they were struck; the fade runs its whole length even if the old voice's own release ends first; a fade outlives a cancelled wait; capPolicy 1 cancels a waiting note that is the oldest held; a polyMode change cancels every waiting note; the keep-phase snapshot is taken at a fade's end from the voice that just ended (the lead's reading, extended to a fade nobody waits on). The two rules in the description (a stolen note keeps its gate; a released waiting note is a tail to the tiers) are PROPOSED and the human's to ratify. (4) AS BUILT, RULE (a) HAS A STEP: an off that comes 239 samples after the take gives the note a gate of 239 samples; one that comes at 240 (on the sample the note starts) or 241 is an ordinary off and gives a gate of 0 or 1 sample, because a note that has started is released at once. A stolen note held longer than the fade still loses the fade's length of its gate. Delaying every off of a stolen note by its wait would remove the step and release such notes 5 ms after the key. (5) THE LEDGER CHECK COULD NOT HEAR THIS DIVERGENCE: its fixed script strikes both notes at sample 0 into an empty pool, where no voice can be taken. ROADMAP B465 gave its scenarios a note script, which this entry's two scripted scenarios use.
